title: Collective-dissipation-induced dark and metastable-like states for enhanced quantum battery performance
authors: Achraf Khoudiri, Asghar Ullah, Abderrahim El Allati, Özgür E. Müstecaplıoğlu
abstract: We investigate the role of symmetry-protected dark states and metastable-like frozen states in the autonomous charging dynamics of open quantum batteries described by a transverse-field Ising model. By comparing local and collective dissipation over a range of system sizes, temperatures, and magnetic phases, we demonstrate that collective dissipation generates symmetry-protected dark states together with a much larger set of frozen (metastable) states, forming an extended protected Hilbert space. We derive the multiplicity of the collective dark sector analytically, showing that it follows the Catalan sequence for even system sizes, while such states are absent for odd sizes. Our results show that collective dissipation can enhance ergotropy and charging power, with its advantage depending on temperature, magnetic phase, and system size. While the number of dark and frozen states is identical in the ferromagnetic and antiferromagnetic phases, the achievable ergotropy differs substantially because of the different spectral locations of these protected states. In particular, the antiferromagnetic configuration exhibits considerably larger extractable work owing to the favorable positioning of the protected subspaces within the many-body energy spectrum. Finally, we analyze the active Hilbert-space fraction and show that metastable protection provides an effective mechanism for suppressing dissipative losses while preserving efficient charging pathways. These results establish the dark-state and frozen-state sectors as key resources for optimizing the performance of open quantum batteries through engineered dissipation.
summary: This paper explores how engineered dissipation can optimize the performance of quantum batteries modeled by the Ising chain. By comparing local versus collective environmental coupling, the authors demonstrate that collective dissipation creates symmetry-protected dark and metastable states. These protected subspaces significantly enhance extractable work (ergotropy), with the antiferromagnetic phase showing superior energy harvesting capabilities.
main_problem: The study investigates how symmetry-protected dark states and metastable frozen states influence the autonomous charging dynamics and overall performance of open quantum batteries.
main_result: Collective dissipation is shown to enhance ergotropy and charging power by generating an extended protected Hilbert space; specifically, the antiferromagnetic configuration yields considerably larger extractable work compared to the ferromagnetic phase.
method: The analysis involves comparing local versus collective dissipation effects on a quantum battery modeled by the transverse-field Ising Hamiltonian using the GKSL master equation framework.
model_or_system: The system is an open quantum battery described by the transverse-field Ising model, $	ext{H}_B$, evolving under a master equation incorporating both local and collective dissipation mechanisms.
key_observables: Ergotropy (extractable work), charging power, multiplicity of dark states (following Catalan sequence for even N), and active Hilbert-space fraction.
main_assumptions: The dynamics are treated under the Markovian approximation, and finite-resource effects are neglected.
figures_summary: Figures compare energy level time evolution and ergotropy over time for collective versus local dissipation in both AFM and FM regimes, highlighting enhanced work extraction with collective coupling.
paper_structure: The paper systematically compares the dynamics under local vs. collective dissipation, derives the multiplicity of dark states analytically, quantifies performance using ergotropy, and concludes by establishing protected sectors as key optimization resources for quantum batteries.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses non-equilibrium thermodynamics in many-body systems, providing concrete mechanisms (dark/frozen states) to enhance energy storage capacity beyond simple thermal considerations, which is highly relevant to open quantum system dynamics.
